Browser journey tests. `tsconfig.json` type-checks them; `support/` provides
their database and deployment fixtures and shared journey helpers.

Infrastructure for browser journeys: isolated databases, deployed application
processes, prepared actor sessions, UI assertions, and checkout-wide ownership
of the E2E suite.

Application HTML templates, theme tokens, ambient request types, and the server
request lifecycle. Child directories hold models, server use cases and
infrastructure, routes, and database tooling.

Tagged application errors and Markdown compilation shared by server operations,
remotes, and components. Storage and request orchestration belong to their
owning directories.

Reusable Svelte presentation, form, dialog, and pagination components. Consumers
supply projections and callbacks; persistence and authorization belong to
callers.

Shared business records, projections, aggregates, and pure functions used by
client and server modules, grouped by business concept.

Models neither obtain external capabilities nor perform observable effects,
including on import. They import no server infrastructure, SvelteKit request
APIs, or component code.

Other directories own related types:

- Repository-specific SQL, row types, transaction mechanisms, and operation
  parameters belong to repositories.
- Use-case dependency, parameter, and result types, and business calculations
  such as the invitation quota, sit beside their use case.
- Page-only projections such as `ArticleDetail` and `CommentView`, and page-size
  choices, belong to remote functions and route handlers.
- Cookie transport data and cookie writers belong to the server request-boundary
  helper.

Runtime composition and request-boundary authentication support. The registry
initializes the database and provider adapters; request helpers in `auth.ts`
manage cookies, OAuth request data, post-sign-in redirect targets, and locals.
Business operations live in use cases and import neither the registry nor the
request helpers.

Request-independent capabilities: GitHub OAuth, DNS TXT lookup, the clock, and
random value generation. Adapters do not import SvelteKit request or cookie
types. Request parsing, OAuth state-cookie validation, and session cookies
belong to `src/lib/server/auth.ts`; account and session decisions belong to use
cases.

PostgreSQL connection construction, schema declarations, inferred storage row
types, and the SQL schema generated from them for local database tooling.
Consumers are repositories, the server composition boundary, and database
management scripts. Business workflows and repository composition belong to
their owning modules.

`database.sql` is the schema that provisioning runs in a newly created template
database, generated from `schema.ts` by `pnpm db:export`; edit `schema.ts` and
regenerate rather than editing it. Its unconditional `CREATE` statements are not
an idempotent migration, so existing databases are not upgraded. It declares no
foreign keys.

Database reads, writes, model mapping, and internal transactions for articles,
bookmarks, comments, invitations, roles, sessions, and users. Each operation is
a standalone exported function that takes `AppDatabase` from
`src/lib/server/db/schema.ts` as its first parameter; operation-specific object
parameters are exported as `XxxParams` beside their function, and shared models
such as `Session` can serve directly as inputs. Importing a module performs no
queries.

Follow the
[repository conventions](../../../../docs/architecture.md#repositories) for
function structure, data shapes, naming, errors, and transactions.

Use cases own permissions, business decisions, quota calculation, and session
lifetime policy; callers own request context, cookies, DNS, and frontend state.
Repositories generate storage identifiers and persistence timestamps, and keep
table constraints and identifier formats intact.

Paginated results echo the requested `pageNumber` and `pageSize`, return empty
`items` past the last page, and read the total `count` and the page rows from
one consistent snapshot. Every operation runs through `wrap` in `utils.ts`,
which logs it and normalizes its failures.

Isolated PostgreSQL databases for repository integration tests. Each test
database is a clone made through the checkout-local provisioning lifecycle, so
tests exercise real SQL and internal transactions without connecting to the
development database. Application code must not import this test-only module.
Importing it performs no I/O.

Server business operations that need external capabilities. Each operation takes
`deps`, only the capabilities it uses, and `params`, the invocation data.
Callers supply trusted authenticated actors, provider identities, parsed URLs,
and request-independent values; request entry points supply `now` from
`adapters/clock.ts`.

Use cases call repository functions with `deps.db`; repositories own
transactions and persistence consistency. Request boundaries own request
context, cookies, redirects, and remote-query refreshes. Use cases read neither
the service registry, environment variables, nor the current time.

Repository and adapter failures propagate. Expected business failures throw
tagged application errors, with field keys for correctable input. Markdown
compilation and business calculations stay inside the operation that needs them;
a separate exported function exists only for a business scenario that several
callers share.

The deterministic shared dataset used by local provisioning and browser
journeys, including relationships and derived interaction counts. Seed types
derive from `src/lib/server/db/schema.ts`; roles and path helpers come from
`src/lib/models`.

The shared application shell, the homepage article list, and the application
error page. Layout and page remote queries supply viewer identity and homepage
data, and components call these queries directly, following the
[initial-data conventions](../../docs/architecture.md#initial-data-and-pagination).

Article detail, direct article responses, comments, and viewer-specific
interaction controls. Remote functions adapt requests and delegate business
authorization to use cases, following the
[request-boundary conventions](../../../../docs/architecture.md#request-boundaries-and-remote-functions).

The article editor: guards article creation and editing, and renders the
Markdown or external-link editor while keeping the reply context. Remote forms
own publication writes and the final redirect, following the
[request-boundary conventions](../../../../../docs/architecture.md#request-boundaries-and-remote-functions).

The sign-in page: separate GitHub OAuth registration and login forms that carry
the requested `next` destination through the OAuth round trip. Outside
production builds it also links to the simulated login in `testing/`.

The GitHub OAuth callback: completes sign-in or account creation, starts a
session, sets its cookie, and returns to the requested destination.

Simulated login for development and tests: pick any stored user and sign in as
them without GitHub. Both remote operations throw FORBIDDEN in a production
build unless the mode is `test`.

The signed-in viewer's settings console. The layout query requires login and
offers only the pages the viewer's roles allow; any other console path,
including `/console` itself, redirects to the first allowed page. Child pages
read the viewer from that same query, and their remotes still enforce
permissions themselves.
Shows the viewer's username and GitHub ID and edits the username in a dialog.
Lets a reader redeem an invite code to become an author.
Lists the viewer's bookmarked articles, paginated, with an empty state.

The author's invitation page: inviter, remaining quota, unused codes with delete
and copy controls, code creation, and invited authors.
Edits the viewer's display name and biography.

The public JSON Feed endpoint. It converts recent articles to feed metadata and
HTML without fetching linked external articles.

HTTP server availability for Fly's internal health checks, reported without
querying external services.

Public writer and reader profiles. The selected collection and page live in the
URL, and the profile owner gets account actions. Remote functions follow the
[request-boundary conventions](../../../../docs/architecture.md#request-boundaries-and-remote-functions).

Checkout-local maintenance commands: the PostgreSQL CLI, the Dockerfile Node
version sync run after Nix updates, and the article-count migration that runs
when imported. `lib/` owns PostgreSQL provisioning, process lifecycle, and
seeding.

Checkout-local PostgreSQL management for development and test callers: the
process lifecycle, seeded template databases, isolated clones, and destructive
resets that run only when explicitly requested.

files.doc:
app.css is the global stylesheet: it loads Tailwind, replaces Tailwind's default color, font, and text scales with
the application theme tokens, and adds the layout and spacing tokens. `--palette-*` values are RGB channels from
Rosé Pine Dawn in light mode and Rosé Pine in dark mode, switched by `prefers-color-scheme`; `--color-*` tokens wrap
them as CSS colors.

random.ts owns the format of every application-generated random value, one named method per purpose, so reviewing
randomness means reading this file. Callers never choose alphabets or lengths.

auth.ts adapts requests for hooks, remote functions, and route handlers: the session and OAuth state cookies,
post-sign-in redirect targets, and `App.Locals`. Models and use cases must not import it. Importing it performs no
database, network, or cookie operation.

schema.ts declares the Drizzle tables and their inferred row types; insert shapes come from each table's
$inferInsert. `createdAt` and `updatedAt` columns are required and default to now. Tables declare no foreign keys.

article.ts reads article models and projections, and inserts and updates persisted articles together with their
direct parent's reply count.

bookmark.ts reads bookmark state and keeps relationship changes consistent with the article's persisted bookmark
count.

comment.ts reads comment records and per-user grouped projections, and inserts and updates comments while keeping
article comment counts consistent.

invite_code.ts persists invitation codes and exposes consistent quota inputs. Quota arithmetic belongs to the
invitation use case.
role.ts reads assigned roles and invitation relationships, and persists invitation redemption atomically.

session.ts persists supplied session data. Use cases own ID generation, current-time reads, expiration decisions,
and renewal policy.
user.ts reads user identity and profile data, and persists supplied profile changes.

utils.ts holds the operation wrapping and storage identifier generation shared by the repositories in this
directory. These helpers are not database operations themselves.

session.ts creates, validates, and invalidates the sessions behind the `auth_session` cookie. A token is
`<id>.<secret>`; only the secret's hash is stored. Cookie handling stays with the caller.

data.ts builds the shared dataset in memory once, on import, with deterministic minute-spaced timestamps starting at
2026-01-01 UTC. Importing it does no database or network work.

postgres.ts controls this checkout's PostgreSQL cluster in .direnv/pg, independently of the caller's working
directory.

migrate_article_counts.ts rewrites article interaction counts as soon as it is imported, writing to the database
configured by the environment. It never closes the database connection.

pg.ts is the checkout-local PostgreSQL CLI and runs its command from `process.argv` when evaluated. `start <name>`
ensures the `exodus-<name>` clone; `reset <name|template>` deletes the named database, or every exodus database for
`template`; `stop` stops PostgreSQL under the control lock; `status` prints the process list as JSON, or
`{ "status": "Stopped" }`. Any other form, including extra arguments, throws the usage message; failures propagate
to the process.

sync-node-version.ts keeps the Dockerfile's `FROM node:<version>-slim AS base` image at the running Node version.
Run it from the repository root inside `nix develop` so the locked development runtime supplies that version;
Renovate runs `--write` after lock file maintenance. `--write` rewrites only that line; `--check` changes nothing and
fails on a mismatch. Invalid arguments and a missing or repeated base image fail in both modes. It uses only Node
built-ins, so it needs no installed dependencies.

before.doc:
Playwright `test` whose journeys each own a database clone, real sessions, a deployment process, and actor contexts.
Each test resets and clones the database that `databaseSuffix` derives from its title, runs `scenario.prepare` on it,
stores a real session for every test-dataset user, and starts `build/index.js` in production mode on its own port
with a matching `APP_URL`, waiting up to 20 seconds for readiness. The adapter derives the local HTTP origin from
`PROTOCOL_HEADER`, so requests must send `x-forwarded-proto: http`: the `extraHTTPHeaders` fixture does, and custom
browser contexts must inherit it. `actor(username)` opens a page in a separate browser context carrying that user's
session cookie. Teardown follows dependency order: contexts close, the application stops (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after
five seconds), then the database connection closes and a passed test's database is deleted. A failed test keeps its
database and attaches its name and the application log.

before.signature: export function acquireSuiteLock(): void
before.doc:
Synchronously acquires the checkout's `.direnv/e2e-suite.lock` before Playwright clears output. The new owner records
its PID and token and exports the token as `EXODUS_E2E_LOCK_TOKEN`, so discovery subprocesses and workers pass when
the owner file holds their inherited token; only the owning process releases the lock, on exit. An existing lock
throws without touching output, and missing or malformed ownership grants nothing. A failure recording ownership
removes the new lock. Abrupt termination can leave a stale lock that needs manual investigation.

before.signature: export async function ensureDatabase(name: string): Promise<void>
before.doc:

1–56 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit; `template` and `all`
are rejected. Runs under the checkout control lock and a PostgreSQL advisory lock, releasing clients and locks on
every exit path. A missing template is created from `template0`, loaded with `src/lib/server/db/database.sql`, and
seeded; its version, a SHA-256 of that schema and `src/lib/testing/data.ts`, is recorded only after both complete.
Existing databases are never reset: an outdated version or a missing initialization record throws with the
`pnpm pg:reset` command to run. Connection environment variables are unchanged. A failure leaves partial databases
for explicit reset.
